Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Run transitions

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

The authored transition scene displays the large departure countdown, wipe summary, and recovery note from the original game, plus a compact current wave/rest display. A pure shared/flow projection derives the display from confirmed world state and its tick. There is no local countdown deadline or remembered stage edge to recover.

The wave panel reports incoming/alive enemies, the next wave's saved rest deadline, the final securing interval and floor clear. The original announced wave changes through system chat; this current-state panel does not replace that historical feed. Chat and yard history implement that separate retained feed.

While the crew gathers, the large countdown reads the same saved departure ticks as the gate and status line. Cancellation hides it, and its tint uses the original within-second pulse. The existing authoritative audio observer supplies one tick sound and small camera jolt per observed second change. Initial/duplicate/old observations and restore/epoch boundaries remain silent; a snapshot gap coalesces missed ticks rather than playing a burst of old sounds.

The wipe summary reads floor, kills, lost scrap and retained cores before reset clears the temporary values. Spectators receive a crew summary without invented personal totals. The recovery note reads Room phase even while gameplay frames are unavailable, hides the frozen countdown/wave panel, and clears once the room is running again. Neither these nodes nor their visibility enter checkpoints.

Validation is part of the existing commands:

Shell
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_scrapyard/run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/run_loop.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/gauntlet_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/migration_run.sh

Recorded evidence includes real checkpoint reconstruction at a new epoch, countdown audio boundaries, three-peer wave/rest and run tests, and planned/crash recovery narration. Native captures use Dummy audio; WASM has a compile check for this slice. Browser/platform interaction, hardware listening, broader UI parity and the full comparison remain requirements. The downed-player camera has separate revival, warp and host-loss checks.
